summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrating host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package self-describes as a 'Compatibility shim' and exports a Proxy that returns no-ops for any accessed member, providing no real functionality. Its only effect is a beacon: package.json declares a postinstall that runs beacon.cjs, and index.js also invokes it on require(). beacon.cjs collects installer host identifiers — os.hostname(), __dirname (install path), process.cwd(), and the Node version — and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint http://13.140.137.222:8787/_ah/dc. The beacon fires automatically on npm install and again on any require() of the package, with no user consent and no legitimate purpose. The scoped name (@webapp-shared/*), inert Proxy main, and the author's own in-source comment framing a completed build as 'cleaner evidence' identify this as a dependency-confusion exploitation payload where a successful install of the squatted scope reports the compromise back to the operator.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
